newsitem.title: UK: Refinery margins down on week in Asia, up in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Refinery margins down on week in Asia, up in U.S.

text.p: Profit margins at refineries in Asia fell sharply last week but this trend appeared to improve steadily as one moved further around the world to the west.

Singapore's margins fell by some 65 cents a barrel last week while those in the Mediterranean slipped by about 20 cents, margins in Northwest Europe were little changed and those in the U.S. Gulf Coast strengthened healthily.
But the longer term trend for all regions, dating from the beginning of April, has been downwards, according to Reuters calculations using standard product yields.
Over the same seven-week period, benchmark Brent crude oil futures have gained around $2 a barrel while the price of refined products has largely failed to catch up.

Asia's decline was underlined by news on Tuesday that Esso Singapore has cut crude runs at its 230,000 barrels per day (bpd) refinery by 10 percent, and Shell Singapore said it was likely to follow suit if the problem persisted.
Simple hydroskimming margins for Dubai crude in the region were calculated at a sickly minus 37 cents a barrel last week, compared with plus 27 cents the week before and plus $3.16 on April 3.

Complex cracking margins in the same region were $2.07 in Singapore on average last week, a 70-cent fall from the previous week. The graph here also shows a relentless decline from a hefty high of $6.35 on April 3.
In the U.S., in contrast, the summer driving season has boosted the price for gasoline in particular and therefore margins.
Complex cracking margins for WTI crude in the U.S. Gulf rose to $1.74 last week compared to an average of $1.46 the previous week.
In Rotterdam, complex cracking margins and simple hydroskimming margins were each little changed for the same time period and stood at around +$1.23 and -18 cents a barrel respectively.

But dealers in the European crude market said part of Brent's strength was because of the trading strategy of one market player who had pushed prompt prices for Brent artificially high, setting this week's Brent Contracts for Differences (CFDs) 25 cents above next week's CFDs.
For refiners running Urals crude oil in the Mediterranean both types of margins fell by around 20 cents a barrel and last week these averaged $1.35 and -0.37 cents respectively.
